card.title: DANUTA
card.text: At the start of your turn, add a 4TP to your support line with Blitz. Destroy it end of turn.
card.flavorText: The Danuta was a Polish armored train used during WWII, primarily in the Invasion of Poland in September 1939. Originally built in 1919, it was part of Poland’s small but effective fleet of armored trains, designed for troop support, and mobile defense. Following Poland’s mobilization in 1939, the Danuta armored train was attached to the Poznań Army. During the initial phase of the invasion, it provided support to Polish infantry units. On September 4th, the train came under attack by Luftwaffe bombers but sustained only minor damage. Later, it took part in the Battle of the Bzura, a major Polish counteroffensive. By 16 September, the Danuta successfully stalled the German 24th Infantry Division’s advance and attempted to retreat toward the Polish 16th Infantry Division. However, it was ambushed by German anti-tank artillery during the withdrawal. Severely damaged and with ammunition nearly exhausted, the train’s commander, Captain Korobowicz, ordered its destruction to prevent capture. The crew detonated the train, inflicting casualties on pursuing German infantry. Amongst the scouting tanks deployed from the train, five TKS tankettes escaped, while two obsolete FT-17 tanks were destroyed to avoid their capture by German forces.
